doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Answering 'what do you do' and the fluctuating income of a musician
summary: Frichtel says he simply answers that he is a musician; he feels fortunate to have made a living at it, though income fluctuates weekly.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: When you meet someone for the first time and they say, “so what do you do” — do you have a short answer?

I have a short answer. I say I’m a musician. And then they go, “but what do you really do.” And I say I’m a musician. And I understand it. Because the music business, it might not be the easiest way to make a living. And a lot of people I think have done it either semi-professionally or where they have a regular day gig or something like that. And I feel incredibly fortunate to have been able to make my living my adult life as a professional musician — either as a player or singing or a composer. It’s been wonderful. Challenging often times, but wonderful.
Yes. Forget about what was my income last year, what was it last week.
